nt: In the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today, this verse begins with the word **Benjamin**. However, a comparison with the other verses in the chapter that introduce the descendants of one of Jacob’s sons suggest that it should begin “The sons of Benjamin.” Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have inadvertently omitted the expression “The sons of” because it consists of the same two consonants as the beginning of the name Benjamin, which may have been written as a separate word. nt: The term that the ULT translates as **Aher** could be: (1) the name of a man. The ULT and UST follow that interpretation. (2) a term that means “another.” That other son of Jacob would be Dan, since [Genesis 46:23](../gen/46/23.md) indicates that Dan had a son named Hushim. The reference in the next verse to the “sons of Bilhah” would support this interpretation, since the two sons of Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali. The author would be reluctant to name Dan because that was the earliest Israelite tribe to become involved in idolatry. Alternate translation: [another son of Jacob] or [Dan]
